differences.text: An element cannot observe whether an author attached a click listener, so `onClick != null` becomes the boolean `pressable` attribute. The native `click` event is emitted; a click on nested interactive content bubbles as its own click (check event.target) instead of being swallowed as in React.
`interactiveRef` (a React ref) is the `interactiveElement` property, or declaratively the `interactive-selector` attribute resolved in the item's light DOM at click time.

Upstream's `role` prop (a parent owns the keyboard access) is the host's own `role` attribute: with one, the row renders no inner button or anchor, treats `pressable` as look-only, and picks aria-selected or aria-current from it.

A click anywhere on a pressable or link row is forwarded to the real button or anchor (ClickableContainerController), so padding, start and end areas navigate a link row, and modifier and middle clicks behave like the link. Upstream forwarded surface clicks to `onClick` only, so the padding of a link row did not navigate.

ItemDescriptionContext published an element id. An IDREF cannot cross the item's shadow root, so the context publishes the description text and, when the author slotted the description, the element (same tree as a slotted control).
The hover fill is the Tecton table-row hover role (--tecton-color-table-row-hover), as in tecton-astryx components.ts `item`; the pressed wash keeps --color-overlay-pressed.
`as` selects semantics only: the host is always one custom element, so `as="li"` is the listitem role through ElementInternals rather than an <li> tag.
